thesis: A slow, warm, hypnotic object: wax blobs that merge, stretch, pinch off and sink in a glowing glass, which you can also run like a real lamp (switch on, wait for heat, tweak).
job: arrive and see a lamp at a glance (glass, base, cap, glow)
switch the lamp on; wax is cold and settled at the bottom
wait while the bulb heats: wax softens, rises, first blob detaches
watch blobs rise, merge, stretch, pinch, cool, sink, repeat
poke the wax: click/drag a blob, stir with the pointer, shake the lamp
change colour pairing (wax and liquid), heat level, blob count/size
switch off: glow fades, wax cools and slumps to the bottom
switch back on and run again; settings persist during the session

principles: wax is viscous so motion is slow and damped
surface tension merges and pinches blobs
heat from the bottom, cooling at the top
tricks: metaball field summed from r^2/d^2 falloff, thresholded
a pool blob at the bottom that is wide and flat
tiny horizontal wander noise so paths never repeat
tests: do blobs ever stall at the top forever
do they ever clump into one mass
does it look different after 2 minutes

principles: low-res field upscaled is soft and cheap
glow comes from layered radial gradients and additive light
steps: render field at ~1/3 resolution to offscreen canvas
shade by field value for a rim highlight
tricks: ImageData per-pixel field with smoothstep threshold gives soft edges
gradient within the blob via field strength gives volume
vertical colour gradient in wax (hotter near bulb)
tests: does the wax look flat or volumetric

principles: silhouette is a tapered glass flask on a metal base and cap
the object reads before the UI does
steps: draw base cone, glass, cap, spill glow
tricks: bulb glow visible at the bottom of the glass
warm light cast on surface below
tests: would a stranger say lava lamp in one second

tricks: double click drops a new blob
tests: does every control change visible state

tricks: clamp dt to avoid jumps after tab switch

parts: glass flask (tapered, narrow top, wider bottom)
wax blobs and a wax pool
expectations: wax sits on bottom when cold
lamp takes minutes to warm in real life

descriptions: flask is a rounded trapezoid: top width ~34 to 42% of bottom
blobs are slightly taller than wide when rising, flat when pooled
behaviors: close blobs merge by field sum

descriptions: wax brighter than liquid; hot end lighter
liquid is a deep saturated tint, darker at top
behaviors: colour pairs: magma red on amber, magenta on violet, lime on teal, ice cyan on navy

descriptions: rise takes 10 to 25 s end to end
warm-up 6 to 15 s in a demo (real lamp 45 min)
behaviors: on: bulb temp ramps, pool softens, blobs peel up
off: temps fall, blobs sink, pool reforms
pointer near blob pushes it away

descriptions: status label shows state and a temperature readout
behaviors: controls update live: heat slider scales buoyancy; blob size slider and count reseed

anti_keywords.not: circles that bounce around like a screensaver
anti_keywords.instead: temperature-driven slow rise and sink with viscous drag
metaball field with soft threshold and shaded volume
cooling near the top so everything returns down

anti_keywords.not: controls that only change a label
anti_keywords.instead: every control alters the simulation or look immediately
on switch starts a warm-up with the wax slumped first

checks: would a stranger say lava lamp at a glance
do blobs visibly merge and pinch
does power off cool and sink the wax, and power on restart it
does every control change the sim
does it work at phone width and with no network
